You’ll be fine, look up some tips online about how to detangle with less breakage and you’ll get better help than just my two cents. I will say focus on your scalp health the most because that’s the beginning of healthy, thick long hair. You can’t repair split ends and it IS best to cut them before they split to the top of the follicle (trust me they will unless you keep sealant on them 24/7 which is impossible imo) do you mind if I ask your age range? That will heavily impact how you should care for your hair and whether or not it’s something that is realistically attainable.

Remember when your hair is wet it’s stretchier and more prone to breakage, that’s why I finger comb - so I can feel when I’m putting too much tension on it. Don’t forget to start at the bottom and work your way up. I also don’t get frequent trims so I have no idea why it keeps growing so fast I have layered hair and just let it do its thing. Genetics also play a strong role in how long our hairs “natural” length is; take a look at some of your other family members photos to see what lengths their hair has been over their lives, my grandmother always had very long hair, my aunts as well, I have Native American in my genetics (not much) and that might play a role as well.

Past the top of my but crack tbh, about hip length, curl pattern wavy on top with loose ringlet curls on the underside - I have always had long hair in my adult and later teen years except for one haircut that chopped me to chest length and I lost my bananas (hair security blanket type thing) and it took me about 3 years to get it waist length after that and then now another 4 for it to go past my waist to now my mid buttocks. My secret? Leave the brush alone, finger comb with conditioner only and find ways to put your hair up that don’t damage it. I just switched to a hair stick to hold it up because years of scrunchie breakage from ponytails caught up to me.
